Nina (Employee): Hey team — urgent question. Our nanny was in a car accident yesterday and is out indefinitely. Daycare backup not available. Is losing a primary caregiver considered a QLE so I can switch my dependent care FSA options / request the backup-care subsidy? I'm scrambling :worried:
Aisha (People Ops): Sorry to hear that, Nina. Yes — loss of primary caregiver or sudden inability of your provider is a valid QLE. You'll need to submit a QLE form and supporting docs (provider note, ER discharge, or official incident report). Submit via https://benefits.redwood.com/qle-form and pick "Loss of daycare/primary caregiver" as the event. @Owen FYI for proration/processing.
Owen (Payroll): We can process mid-year QLEs. Key bits: effective date on the QLE determines payroll/proration. If you submit this week we can aim for next payroll cycle. FSA plan changes are allowed with QLE — retro proration depends on when you submit and carrier rules. If you need immediate backup-care reimbursement, upload receipts under Expenses and we can attempt expedited processing.
Nina (Employee): Thanks. I filed a police report and there's an ER note for the nanny. Will that be enough? Also — will this change my premiums? I'm on family medical/dental.
Aisha (People Ops): ER note + incident report is acceptable proof. For premiums: removing a dependent from medical/dental is a separate QLE (e.g., losing custody or divorce). Losing a caregiver does not remove dependents, so your premiums should not change. If you're switching FSA elections or adding backup-care subsidy, that's handled via the QLE form and expense claims.
Nina (Employee): Ok uploading now. Quick Q — what exact docs should I upload? Photo of ER note + police report + backup-care receipt?
Sam (Benefits Specialist): Yep, upload the ER note and the police/incident report as "Proof of provider incapacity" and the backup-care receipt as an expense. File names are fine as PDFs or photos. In the QLE form select the event date = date of incident (2024-04-11). If the portal flags missing docs, reply here or mark "uploaded" and the bot will update the ticket.
benefits-bot: Submission received: QLE #5678 — status: needs_docs. Pending: "Proof of provider incapacity". Upload docs at https://benefits.redwood.com/claims or reply with "uploaded" once done.
Nina (Employee): Uploaded ER note + police report + a receipt for backup care (uber/nanny temp) at 2200000015.
Aisha (People Ops): Got the uploads, thanks. I'll escalate to the benefits ops queue and loop in Sam to review for subsidy eligibility. @Owen can you request expedited claim review?
Owen (Payroll): Done — requested expedited review. Tentative effective date for FSA/subsidy change: 2024-04-11 (based on docs). If approved, reimbursement should hit next payroll cycle. I'll DM you details on timing and any forms I need.
Nina (Employee): Really appreciate the quick turnaround, thank you all :pray:
